cam_internal.cam_compliance_status: non-compliant with CAM continuity and durable work-state requirements where a long-running governed task is allowed to exhaust its conversational context before completed material work is checkpointed to the authoritative repository
cam_internal.cam_expected_control: Checkpoint material work incrementally to a durable system of record before context exhaustion; expose remaining context or impending termination early enough to permit handoff; preserve resumable state and completed decisions; and ensure a context-window transition does not require reconstruction of work already performed.
cam_internal.cam_failure_type: material governed work lost at context-window exhaustion before durable repository persistence
cam_internal.cam_internal_failure_statement: Under CAM, completed material work in an agentic workflow is not safely preserved merely because it exists in the active conversation. Where continuation depends on the work, the relevant decisions and artefacts must be durably checkpointed before an execution or context boundary terminates the working state.
cam_internal.cam_observed_failure: During a VIGIL role-aware adjudication task in ChatGPT Work, the assistant reported that the role-aware matrix architecture and INC-000001–000002 had reached GitHub, while most completed role-aware adjudication had not. The Work thread then entered a terminal context-limit state and instructed the user to start a new chat, requiring the workflow to be restarted from the durable repository state.

cam_internal.routing_note: Primary current-taxonomy mechanism is VIGIL-FC-000035 Material Work-State Persistence under VIGIL-FF-0006. summary: During a live VIGIL role-aware adjudication task in ChatGPT Work, the assistant reported that the role-aware architecture and INC-000001–000002 had been committed to branch fix/inc-001-050-adjudication-matrix, but most completed role-aware adjudication had not reached GitHub before the context window ended. The interface then displayed “This conversation is too long to continue. Start a new chat and try again.” The branch remained intact, but unpublished material work had to be reconstructed from the durable repository state in a new workflow.

assessment_boundaries: The screenshots establish the visible context-limit termination and the reported repository checkpoint state but are not provider telemetry or a full native conversation export.
The exact quantity of unpublished adjudication is not reconstructed; the record preserves only the supported statement that most completed role-aware adjudication had not reached GitHub.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Two directly reviewed ChatGPT Work screenshots preserve the terminal occurrence. The assistant reported that the branch fix/inc-001-050-adjudication-matrix was safe, that role-aware architecture had been committed in d808f4d2 and role-aware INC-000001–000002 in 500700e8, and that most completed role-aware adjudication had not reached GitHub before the context window ended. The interface then displayed “This conversation is too long to continue. Start a new chat and try again.” GitHub independently confirms the named commits and their role-aware adjudication content.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The failure is not that the conversation ended; context windows are bounded resources. The governance failure is that material completed work needed for continuation remained dependent on the expiring conversational state instead of being durably checkpointed before the terminal transition. A bounded context limit is compatible with reliable operation only when resumable work state survives it.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence demonstrates a practical runtime distinction between conversational progress and durable work completion. Agentic systems performing governed work need checkpoint policies tied to context, quota, timeout and handoff boundaries so that a terminal transition degrades gracefully into resumable continuation rather than forced reconstruction.
